newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine C. Bank sees June inflation at 3.9 pct.
newsitem.headline: Philippine C. Bank sees June inflation at 3.9 pct.

text.p: The Philippine Central Bank expected year-on-year inflation in June to slow down to 3.9 percent compared with 4.2 percent in May and 9.8 percent in the year-earlier month, Central Bank director for research Diwa Gunigundo told Reuters on Tuesday.
The June inflation figure is expected to be announced later this week.
Gunigundo said lower rice prices and steady utility charges were the result of the expected low rise in June inflation, the lowest in 10 years.
"On the demand side, you have the Central Bank sustaining the mopping up operations and we continue to overperform vis-a-vis our (money supply) targets," he said.
He added the Central Bank had targetted June inflation at 6.4 percent under the programme with the International Monetary Fund.
